question: Can a sparse real-space bound plus the positive-semidefinite reciprocal PME contribution certify the frozen normalized relative spectral condition without a dense whole-system matrix?
current_spectral_criterion: lambda_min(Dbar)>1e-6*lambda_max(Dbar)>0 with Dbar=sqrt(alpha) D sqrt(alpha); no threshold change
domain: one metal, conducting boundary, positive active alpha; zero-alpha sites excluded from unknowns
native MUTUAL/Thole and exact native POLPAIR/group scaling
orthorhombic or general nondegenerate periodic cell only if actual qfac nonnegative and scatter/gather adjoint
no replica self-image real-space terms until explicitly included; native real cutoff smaller than half shortest periodic image

real_space_derivation.T_real_pair: rr3 I + rr5 r r^T from umutual2a/2b after exact dampewald, dampthole and uscale
real_space_derivation.diagonal_atom_block: B_ii=I+alpha_i H_ii-alpha_i*tself*I, adjusted for any admitted within-site terms
real_space_derivation.block_extension: The same inequalities hold for fixed disjoint molecular blocks; internal interactions belong in diagonal block, each cross-block counted once per incident block. No eigenvalue clipping or functional changes.

reciprocal_hypothesis.needed_source_proof: Actual grid_uind and fphi_uind are adjoints after Cartesian/fractional maps, exact FFT normalization, qfac>=0. Then R is PSD; no physical assumption that arbitrary PME implementation is PSD.
reciprocal_hypothesis.bounds: If R PSD and norm2(R)<=U_rec, lambda_min(Dbar)>=L_real and lambda_max(Dbar)<=U_real+U_rec. Include declared numerical uncertainty margins before using these inequalities.
reciprocal_hypothesis.failure_meaning: Insufficient bound is inconclusive, not proof of unstable Hamiltonian; no fallback that silently admits a solve.

ownership.Arendt: actual PME adjoint/sign/normalization and computable upper-norm bound
ownership.Planck: declared saved six-vacuum-matrix atom/molecule block-bound feasibility
